why: D3a-01 set that the candidates are decided by their own D2 lines, and that no rule binds them; the arrow rule decides only what the account may say an element brings about. P19 entered at C2a-03 as a candidate; F-012 found that hosting follows neither help, coalition nor upkeep, and its bound found the declared order reversed in 16 of 21 rooms. P19 drew 787 lines in 689 rooms, every one ruled under G57 and its 13 readings (D3a-53). 477 lines show it, in 382 rooms: a host rules on requests (approves, denies, sets conditions, lists or removes works) in 274, a guest asks the room that holds the space in 221, a small room seeks or is promised a bigger room's protection in 50, and members dispute who may approve in 57. In 82 rooms the lines show only a request, with no ruling, protection or dispute; P19's range runs from a single request, so these rooms show it. The room is the host in 114 rooms and the guest in 273. In 340 of the 382 rooms the room's own members act; in 42 only a visitor acts for its own room (G18). 10 rooms show it only after the close, and 6 only in NONPORTABLE particulars. No line corrects P19: the 60 restrict lines narrow it to granted, enforced, lasting or binding rule, which its range does not claim (G9), so 57 are specifications and 3 evidence limits. Of the 60 add lines, 54 add steps, conditions or links its statement holds, one a link that P13 states, two a paired link (below), one is a NONPORTABLE particular, one is one room's particular (tokyo-013, a canvas judged too full), and one is an evidence limit. Of the 217 instantiate lines, 213 show it, 3 do not, and 1 is a NONPORTABLE particular that shows it. 142 of the 450 absent lines fail because their concepts show it, and 297 stay evidence limits. By reading 13, a request or leave to build beside another room's work stays P08's, so P19 keeps its edge with borders and deals. Most rooms that show P19 also show P08 (352) and P16 (360), which are broad, but the acts differ: asking the room that holds the space and its ruling are not a border or help. No arrow is grounded and none is claimed, so the account may say what guests and hosts did and claims no effect of P19; F-012 and its bound stand, since P19 claims no order, and two lines show the work laid before the host was asked (gamindustri-017, puzzleanddragons-041). The census shows one edge, which I carry to the clustering rather than revise here: the host is a colour faith in 131 rooms, and in 90 of the 274 rooms with a ruling; 12 of K04's 22 colour-faith rooms are P19 hosts. Two link lines make a host's ruling depend on its faith (orderofthebluecorner-040, thebluecorner-066), but both are subs of one faction, so the pair is thin as a second room. This is the head's contrary condition, a faith deciding whom a room admits, and it may make a cluster branch of P19 beside K04's faith branch. The statement and range stand as written. The words served to every room in the return are unchanged, so the re-admission rewrites no text a room adapted to; the re-check scope is set when the re-check is built.
